title: Season 5: Rage of the Frostborn Patch Notes
tldr: Season 5: Rage of the Frostborn (patch 1.5) is built around Rage of Morditas, a timed kill-streak encounter whose loot you shape with blood and ice rituals. It leads to a new Morditas boss and a pinnacle fight that requires 400 Corruption. Paladin, Shaman and Bladedancer each get a new skill, and the patch adds 16 uniques and 2 set items. The Bazaar and Circle of Fortune get big reworks, many Runic Invocation combos are buffed, and early corrupted loot and repeated echo farming are toned down.
highlights: Rage of Morditas: a timed kill-streak encounter with ritual-driven loot and 18 exclusive item bases
New Morditas boss, plus Demigod's Ascendance, a pinnacle fight that requires 400 Corruption
New skills: Radiant Lance (Paladin), Summon Tide Elemental (Shaman) and Dreamslash (Bladedancer)
Bazaar price suggestions with automatic price lowering; Circle of Fortune prophecies rebuilt around rewards you choose
16 new uniques, 2 set items and a large Runic Invocation buff pass

changes.text: A new timed encounter starts at a Blood Crystal in the Campaign or Monolith; kills extend the clock, then the enemies you killed rise again for a second wave.
Reaching 20, 50, 90, 140 and 200 kills earns a charge plus a random buff from a pool of 28, and the charges are then spent to claim or reroll item rewards.
Morditas loot can roll new Ice Forging Potential, which may be kept when crafting, or Blood Forging Potential, which raises critical craft chance.
18 new level-50 item subtypes drop only from Rage of Morditas.
Repeated Morditas encounters in the Monolith unlock special Echoes that end in a Morditas boss fight; an adjustable Anger level raises both difficulty and loot.
Beating Morditas awards Demigod's Ascendance, a Pinnacle Woven Echo that requires 400 Corruption.
16 new unique items and 2 new set items are added to the loot pool.
Radiant Lance (15 Paladin points) requires a shield, fires a lightning beam, and gains 1% more damage for each 1% of uncapped block chance.
Summon Tide Elemental (30 Shaman points) adds a permanent cold-spell minion with a Geyser on a 4-second cooldown.
Dreamslash (10 Bladedancer points) is a 3-mana dash-and-slash attack that your Shadows also perform.
Listings get a suggested price based on recent sales, and sellers can opt in to automatic price drops (hourly, daily or weekly) down to a floor they set.
All equippable item types can be bought at any rank, ranks now unlock bags of crafting materials or keys, and Black Market tokens are removed.
Prophecy rerolling is gone: you choose a reward for each of 4 slots, the slots store up to 99 charges as you earn Favor, and new purchasable Lenses modify them.
Echoes you have already attempted now award much less XP and favor when you enter them again.
Pre-corrupted drops can no longer carry T7 affixes until area level 80, or T6 affixes until area level 50.
Omen Windows now appear from area level 18 (from 10), and their Idol Altar drop chance is now 40% at area levels 32-49 and 80% at 50-79 (from 100%).
Synchronized Strike now needs 35 Bladedancer points (from 10), and Symbols of Hope needs 35 Paladin points (from 15).
Many invocations hit harder; for example, Dragons' Breath goes from 300% to 600% effectiveness and Antipode of Mesembria from 900% to 1,500%.
Mana cost drops from 16 to 12, and melee damage effectiveness rises from 100% to 200%.
The ward-per-second affix on rings and amulets is lower; for example, tier 1 now rolls 2-3 (from 6-7).
Enemies and Echo rewards drop imprinted items about 20% more often, and Lost Caches about 40% more often.
A new Nexus panel shows endgame activities, timelines, dungeons and factions, and Echo of the World is renamed Traveler's Rest and gets a waypoint.
Full Offline mode now starts from the game's landing page instead of a Steam launch option, and controller users get native menu navigation instead of a virtual cursor.
